territorial_scope.description: Amends the EAR's VEU list, which governs exports, reexports and in-country transfers of items subject to the EAR to listed facilities in China, by removing three named facilities.

summary.short: US Bureau of Industry and Security final rule removing Intel Semiconductor (Dalian) Ltd, Samsung China Semiconductor Co. Ltd and SK hynix Semiconductor (China) Ltd from the Validated End-User authorization list in Supplement No. 7 to part 748 of the EAR. Effective December 31, 2025. Affects exports to those facilities.
summary.long: A final rule of the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), U.S. Department of Commerce, amends the Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR Part 748) to revise the Validated End-User (VEU) Authorizations list for the People's Republic of China. It removes three facilities, Intel Semiconductor (Dalian) Ltd, Samsung China Semiconductor Co. Ltd and SK hynix Semiconductor (China) Ltd, by deleting their entries under China from Supplement No. 7 to part 748. The rule states that the End-User Review Committee determined the removals under § 748.15 and supplement no. 9 to part 748. It is effective December 31, 2025. BIS cites Section 1762(a) of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 as allowing the change to be imposed in a final rule without prior notice and comment, and estimates an additional 1,000 license applications annually as a result of the removals. The document as fetched also contains unrelated Federal Register rules (a Syria rule under § 746.9 and a Department of Labor rescission), which are outside this annotation.

notes: The source file contains three Federal Register rules: a Syria revision of section 746.9, this China VEU removal rule (annotated in full: preamble and the removal in Supplement No. 7 to Part 748), and a Department of Labor WIA regulation rescission (not annotated). The rule states an effective date of December 31, 2025 and was issued without notice and comment under ECRA section 1762(a). The text contains no obligations, thresholds or enforcement provisions; its only operative change is the removal of three VEU entries. The registry status in_force cannot be confirmed from this text beyond the stated effective date.

evidence.quote: Validated End-Users (VEUs) are designated entities located in eligible destinations to which eligible items subject to the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) may be exported,

thresholds.note: The text contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Numbers present are the effective date (2025-12-31), PRA burden estimates (1,000 applications, 495 hours, 29.7 minutes) and the Federal Register citation, none of which sets scope, eligibility or consequences.

enforcement.note: No sanction regime, penalty amount, criminal penalty, or cure period is stated in this text. The rule removes three named PRC entities from the VEU program (Supplementary Information, Part II) without stating a sanction or grounds. Paperwork Reduction Act paragraph 2 only says no person is subject to a penalty for failing to respond to a collection of information lacking a valid OMB control number. ECRA is cited as legal basis, but its penalty provisions are not reproduced here.

obligations.note: The rule's only operative text removes three entries from Supplement No. 7 to part 748; it places no new duty in its own words. The practical effect (suppliers to the three facilities need licenses under the general EAR requirements; BIS estimates about 1,000 extra applications a year) follows from other EAR provisions not reproduced here. The Syria (§ 746.9) provisions in the fetched file belong to a different rule (FR Doc. 2025-16724) and are not annotated.
